questions.q: What makes Azure Cloud Shell different from running the az CLI or Az module locally?
options: It runs in the browser with the CLI and Az module already pre-installed, nothing to set up
It only supports a read-only, non-scriptable set of commands
It requires its own separate paid subscription to use
It replaces the az CLI and Az module entirely with a new syntax
questions.explain: Cloud Shell runs in the Azure Portal (or shell.azure.com) on a temporary machine Microsoft manages, with both the CLI and Az module already installed in either the Bash or PowerShell flavor.

questions.q: What actually persists between two separate Cloud Shell sessions?
options: The underlying virtual machine running the shell
Only commands typed in the most recent 20 minutes
Nothing at all persists between sessions
Files saved in $HOME, because it's mounted from a persistent Azure Files share
questions.explain: The compute running Cloud Shell is temporary and rebuilt each session, but $HOME is mounted from a persistent Azure Files share, so saved files survive.

questions.q: Roughly how long can Cloud Shell sit idle before the session disconnects?
options: About 24 hours
About 5 minutes
About 20 minutes
It never times out
questions.explain: Cloud Shell disconnects after roughly 20 minutes of inactivity; files on the mounted share are unaffected, but anything still running in that shell is not.

questions.q: In the Bash loop `for rg in $(az group list --query "[].name" --output tsv); do ... done`, what does `--output tsv` make possible?
options: Automatic deletion of each resource group as it's listed
Plain, header-free rows the shell's for loop can iterate over cleanly
Nothing — tsv output cannot be used inside a script
A graphical table the loop renders on screen
questions.explain: tsv output strips headers and formatting down to plain rows, which is exactly what a shell loop needs to iterate over one item at a time.

questions.q: Why would you choose your local CLI or PowerShell install over Cloud Shell for a script meant to run unattended every night?
options: Local installs are required before Azure will accept any CLI command
Cloud Shell cannot run az or Az module commands at all
Cloud Shell's temporary compute and session timeout make it a poor fit for unattended, scheduled scripts
Scheduled scripts can only run inside the Azure Portal itself
questions.explain: Cloud Shell is built for interactive, browser-based sessions with a timeout and temporary compute — not for scripts that need to run unattended on a recurring schedule.
